issues.issue: Original first-edition chapter is printed LXXXVIII but research editorial sequence calls it LXXXIX due a duplicated prior numeral.
Chapter LXXXIX editorial occupies original PDF493/printed459; Twelfth House and printed LXXXIX begin PDF494/printed460.
The first and eleventh house relationships are generic horary rules without any named or independently followed friends.
Favorable application by sextile or trine is distinct from adverse square and opposition; opposition is called worse than square.
Joining in friendship, mutual respect and affection, and absence of quarrels are different human outcomes.
Secret wishes without a named object are treated differently from an explicitly named desire judged by its own topical house.
Success for a secret wish requires favorable planets in angular or succedent houses, not any benefic anywhere.
The love-of-two subsection uses 11th, 7th, and 3rd lords, and a twelfth-house interference exception.
The wording about inward affection versus an outward show cannot establish a real person's concealed feelings.
A favorable condition regarding absence of a twelfth-house aspect and an enhanced condition involving all three houses are distinct.
Fixed signs are given extra firmness, without quantitative or independently demonstrated psychological effect.
Exact aspect application, sign locations and house rulers were not recalculated against a dated historical chart.
The source page provides neither verifiable respondent identity, frozen prediction, blinded questionnaire, comparator nor follow-up.
No modern relationship or psychological validity follows from the 1647 source cataloguing; no model runtime promotions.
